extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO/OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules applied in USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) disciplinary proceedings, including service, default, definitions of professional misconduct, cooperation obligations, and factors for imposing sanctions (exclusion/suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of service of complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint may be served on a respondent by (1) delivering a copy personally; (2) mailing by 'Express Mail,' first-class mail, or any delivery service that provides ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery to the address provided to OED pursuant to § 11.11; or (3) by any method mutually agreeable to the OED Director and the respondent. 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(1)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the decision: use of certified mail, UPS Next Day Air, regular mail, and email; confirmed UPS delivery or respondent's acquiescence to delivery method can satisfy service; sending courtesy copies by other means noted. Failure to personally sign a delivery slip does not preclude finding of proper service if delivery is confirmed or respondent acknowledges receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant obligation to provide and update contact information (37 C.F.R. § 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered attorney/agent must notify the OED Director of postal office address, e-mail addresses, and business telephone number, and every change to any of said addresses or telephone number within thirty days of the date of the change. 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service sent to the address and email provided pursuant to § 11.11 is presumptively effective; the decision relies on the respondent's provided address and email for service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file answer / default admission (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every allegation in the complaint that is not denied by a respondent in the answer shall be deemed to be admitted and may be considered proven; failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations and may result in entry of default judgment. 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.36(d)-(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where respondent fails to answer or otherwise appear, hearing officer need receive no further evidence with respect to admitted allegations; default may lead to sanctions including exclusion. The decision finds respondent in default and deems allegations admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing officer's control of motion response time (37 C.F.R. § 11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules provide that the hearing officer determines the time period in which a response to a motion must be filed. 37 C.F.R. § 11.43.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In default contexts where the respondent has not answered or appeared, it may not be necessary to allow time for response (citing Bovard v. Uland), though as a courtesy extra time may be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to cooperate with OED investigations (37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct impose an obligation to cooperate with OED in an investigation of any matter before it and proscribe knowingly failing to respond to a request from OED. 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED may draw an adverse inference under 37 C.F.R. § 11.23 if respondent does not respond; failure to produce requested bank records and tax documents supports adverse findings and is an independent basis for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider in imposing sanctions (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the appropriate sanction or penalty, the Tribunal must consider: (1) whether the practitioner has violated a duty owed to a client, the public, the legal system, or the profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of the actual or potential injury caused by the practitioner's misconduct; and (4) the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors. 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b) (2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision applies these four considerations (citing fiduciary duties, intentionality, harm to clients by abandonment, and applicable aggravating/mitigating factors) to support exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of significant Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8) / § 11.104(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to inform a client of correspondence received from the Office when the correspondence could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, is received by the practitioner on behalf of a client, and is correspondence which a reasonable practitioner would believe the client should be notified of. (Cited as violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to notify client of notices of withdrawal/abandonment of PCT or US applications; not informing client of notices to file missing parts or fee deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misappropriation or failure to properly remit client funds (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Misappropriation of, or failure to properly or timely remit, funds received by a practitioner from a client to pay a fee which the client is required to pay to the Office. Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision cites depositing client checks and later dishonored checks, failure to forward required filing fees to USPTO, and commingling concerns; such conduct supports severe sanctions including exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglect of a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner by failing to receive or address USPTO communications that led to withdrawal or abandonment of an application. Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include failing to respond to invitations to correct defects, Notices of Missing Parts, or Notices of Incomplete Reply, resulting in abandonment and inability to revive applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to seek client's lawful objectives through reasonable available means (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonable available means in the prosecution of an application. Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where attorney did not timely pay fees or pursue revival where possible, thereby failing to use reasonable means to protect clients' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to carry out a contract of employment for professional services (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to carry out a contract of employment entered into with a client for professional services (i.e., not performing agreed prosecution actions). Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: accepting payment and then allowing matters to lapse without notice or action; failure to perform contracted filing or fee payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prejudice or damage to a client (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Causing prejudice or damage to a client during the professional relationship (e.g., inability to revive applications, loss of intellectual property rights). Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision emphasizes actual loss of clients' valuable IP rights as a significant injury factor for sanction determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (for example, misrepresenting the status of an application and failing to provide an accounting). Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision treats deliberate misrepresentations to clients about fee payment and application status as especially serious, often warranting the most severe sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client by failing to reply to USPTO correspondence or submit required fees. Cited violation: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to conduct after the 2013 Rules amendments; similar to neglect but under the modern Rules of Professional Conduct context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to consult and to keep client reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to reasonably consult with the client about the means to accomplish the client's objectives, and failure to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter. Cited violations: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes not informing clients about abandonment or withdrawal and not responding to client requests for explanations or documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse inference for non-cooperation and reference to Baxter v. Palmigiano
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner does not respond to OED requests for information, the Committee on Discipline may draw an adverse inference in making a determination under 37 C.F.R. § 11.23; courts have allowed adverse inference where respondent refuses to cooperate (citing Baxter v. Palmigiano, 425 U.S. 308 (1976)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision notes OED's explicit warning in RFIs that failure to respond could lead to adverse inferences; respondent's delays and non-production of bank and tax records bolstered the Director's case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ABA Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions (aggravating/mitigating factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior PTO decisions reference the ABA Standards which list aggravating and mitigating factors to consider when imposing sanctions; the Tribunal may apply aggravating factors such as pattern of misconduct, multiple offenses, bad faith obstruction, and failure to show remorse; lack of prior discipline may be considered mitigating but can be outweighed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision identifies four aggravating factors it finds applicable: (1) pattern/multiple offenses; (2) multiple clients harmed; (3) bad faith obstruction of investigations (refusal to produce records); (4) failure to acknowledge wrongdoing or show remorse. The Director's citing of ABA Standards guides sanction severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent and comparators for sanctioning (prior PTO and state cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior PTO disciplinary decisions and state court bar disciplinary decisions are relevant comparators for sanctions — similar misconduct has resulted in exclusion, lengthy suspension, or disbarment (citing Shippey, Goldstein, Gaudio, Hormann, state cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision relies on prior cases where abandonment, dishonesty, and failure to cooperate led to exclusion or long suspensions to justify a similar penalty here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available: exclusion/suspension and publication; duties post-exclusion (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies include exclusion or suspension from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and non-patent matters; excluded practitioners have duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and may petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60. The facts and circumstances of proceedings are to be published in the USPTO official publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director requested exclusion and the Tribunal granted exclusion, citing seriousness of misconduct; additional relief not specified was denied as facts were not precise enough to warrant other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default decision evidentiary posture (no further evidence required for admitted allegations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In default, 'Every allegation in the complaint that is not denied...shall be deemed to be admitted and may be considered proven. The hearing officer at any hearing need receive no further evidence with respect to that allegation.' 37 C.F.R. § 11.36(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision treats admitted allegations as proven and bases findings of liability and sanction on admitted facts and documentary evidence; respondent's non-participation strengthened the Director's showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seriousness threshold: abandonment and deliberate dishonesty justify severe sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of a case or client after being paid for legal services is a significant ethical violation and deliberate dishonesty to clients warrants the most severe sanctions (including disbarment or exclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision references case law and PTO precedents holding that accepting fees and allowing abandonment or making deliberate misrepresentations are grounds for exclusion; the Tribunal applies this guideline to imposition of exclusion here.
